124: function gradientStop(value: string): GradientStop | undefined {
125:   const match = value.match(/^\s*(transparent|rgba?\([^)]*\)|#[\da-f]{3,8})(?:\s+(.+))?\s*$/i);
126:   const parsed = cssColorWithOpacity(match?.[1], true);
127:   if (!parsed) return undefined;
128:   // Percentages map directly to Penpot's normalized stop offsets. Pixel and
129:   // length-based positions depend on the rendered gradient line, which is
130:   // not available in the scene document, so retain CSS's interpolated offset
131:   // for those cases rather than inventing an incorrect absolute position.
132:   const percentage = match?.[2]?.match(/(?:^|\s)(-?\d+(?:\.\d+)?)%/);
133:   const offset = percentage ? clampOpacity(Number(percentage[1]) / 100) : undefined;
134:   return { ...parsed, offset };

137: function resolvedGradientOffsets(stops: GradientStop[]): number[] {
138:   const offsets = stops.map((stop) => stop.offset);
139:   if (offsets[0] === undefined) offsets[0] = 0;
140:   if (offsets[offsets.length - 1] === undefined) offsets[offsets.length - 1] = 1;
141:   // CSS's color-stop fixup first clamps every explicit stop against its
142:   // previous explicit/effective position. Only then are runs of omitted
143:   // positions interpolated, so an omitted stop never creates a backwards
144:   // segment that gets flattened after the fact.
145:   let previous = 0;
146:   for (let index = 0; index < offsets.length; index += 1) {
147:     if (offsets[index] !== undefined) {
148:       previous = Math.max(previous, clampOpacity(offsets[index] as number));
149:       offsets[index] = previous;
150:     }
151:   }
152:   for (let index = 0; index < offsets.length; index += 1) {
153:     if (offsets[index] !== undefined) continue;
154:     let next = index + 1;
155:     while (next < offsets.length && offsets[next] === undefined) next += 1;
156:     const start = offsets[index - 1] as number;
157:     const end = offsets[next] as number;
158:     const count = next - index + 1;
159:     for (let fill = index; fill < next; fill += 1) offsets[fill] = start + (end - start) * (fill - index + 1) / count;
160:     index = next;
161:   }
162:   return offsets as number[];
163: }

181: function cssGradient(value: string | undefined): Gradient | undefined {
182:   const normalized = value?.trim().toLowerCase();
183:   const type = normalized?.startsWith("linear-gradient") ? "linear" : normalized?.startsWith("radial-gradient") ? "radial" : undefined;

185:   const source = value as string;
186:   const parts = cssFunctionArguments(source);

188:   // be understood: filtering failed stops would silently change a gradient's

190:   const stopParts = gradientStop(parts[0]) ? parts : gradientPrelude(type, parts[0]) ? parts.slice(1) : [];

194:   const offsets = resolvedGradientOffsets(colors);

- Surviving-ancestor parenting already worked: I probed zero-size wrappers, `visibility: hidden` with a revived child, and nested `display: contents` — text, elements, and DOM order all land on the correct surviving node, hidden text stays absent. - `src/importer/penpot.ts` — collapsed wrappers (single child, no backdrop) now keep the child's name/source/plugin data; only the wrapper's compositing opacity still multiplies on.
- `src/importer/penpot.test.ts` — new test: wrapper collapsing onto a clipping board keeps the clip's identity with wrapper opacity applied; updated the generated opacity-scene test to assert the surviving child source, 0.25 opacity, and no `#nested-opacity` rename trace.
